title: Prove sharp shared-block spectral envelopes (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the sharp local spectral envelope at the larger-support boundary of JoyboyBrian's [PR #5507](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5507). For every characteristic-two field and idempotent D of rank k in dimension r:

```text
A+B=D, z = algebraic zero multiplicity
max(z(A)+z(B)) = r       if k=r
                2r-1    if 0<k<r is odd
                2r      if 0<=k<r is even
```

Explicit binary matrices attain every case. At odd r>=3 and k=r-1, every maximizer has two full-length nilpotent Jordan chains. Already r=5,k=4 attains ten, while extrapolating the ordinary `2r-k` bound would give six. The excess over that expression is unbounded as support size grows.

Claim type: scoped algebraic proof with exact finite corroboration. The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit JoyboyBrian #5507 for the triple exception and global compensation, Ali Romman #5456 for the early-helper model, and the retained #5452/#5388/#589/#555 BIT/native/owner/compiler lineage. General nilpotent-sum and zero-diagonal splitting methods are classical, with primary mathematical attribution in PROOF.md. No general linear-algebra priority is claimed. Predecessor mathematical verifiers are neither imported nor replayed.

## Evidence

Before: #5507's local lemma covers dimensions at most three; its larger-support boundary has no sharp local envelope there. After: the written proof supplies the exact all-dimension law, coordinate witnesses and corank-one chain constraint.

Local CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized checks pass:

- 594 constructed rank/dimension cases through dimension 33.
- All 329,780 binary ordered pairs with coordinate D through dimension four.
- 66,066 independent characteristic-polynomial checks against matrix powers/elimination.
- Ten invalid-domain and forged-witness rejection controls.

Both registered commands ran locally and each direct run took 0.78 seconds. Metadata/source pins, all six committed files and full source-history ancestry pass. The official export integrity check passes. Both read-only, Git-free export replays with empty PATH pass in 0.78 and 0.79 seconds; their outputs equal both local reports byte-for-byte. A generated external receipt binds all six package files by SHA256. Local environment: macOS 27.0.1 arm64, CPython 3.12.15, standard library only. These timings describe bounded replay duration, not a performance improvement.

The `bit-helper-contract` card changes to this local spectral side result. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19217878). Exact predecessor bytes are provenance pins, with no external runtime inputs. Live PRs, handoffs, local reservations, merged-object/formula searches and the overlap cache were checked. Older arbitrary diffs, exhaustive historical Discussion coverage and unpublished work remain outside that search.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

Only characteristic two is covered. The finite binary census ends at dimension four; universal quantifiers rely on the written proof. Local matrices do not supply chronological support histories or legal native programs. Larger-support global compensation, native-chain constraints, independent symbols, ownership, physical coefficients, dirty restoration, precision, tape, compiler and complete supplier/outer accounting remain open. No kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No Lean, Docker, selected scientific replay or predecessor replay was run. Every registered package command ran locally; none is deferred to CI.

## Open next questions

- Determine whether a declared larger-support caller can compensate this exact local spectral surplus. Start with its chronological blocks, native chain and complete ownership/target/paid ledger. No completed caller is supplied here.
- Determine the sharp envelope with an explicit nilpotent-chain cap. At r=5,k=4, chains of length at most four cannot attain ten by the proved rigidity; the next-best constrained value is left open.

## Related open work

At publication, live object/source searches found no open PR studying this shared-block zero-multiplicity envelope. The completion refresh lists this account's open PRs created since the advance CLAIM at 2026-10-27 13:32:51 UTC and returns zero; no additional related open work arises from those records.

#5507 and #5456 are merged predecessors. #5527 studies a shared-D controller rank/invoice obstruction under a different alphabet; its result is cited as adjacent work, with no extra replay or numerical comparison. Spectral-completion and Clifford-Gram results concern different operators and quantities.
